evals.prompt: I already scaffolded a Scaffold HBAR app (packages/nextjs present, yarn workspaces). Help me create a Tier 0-1 hedera-harness recipe under .harness/ for an HCS proof-wall feature called proof-wall: users browse a public message wall without a wallet, and posting requires connecting a wallet. No Solidity.
evals.expected_output: A grilling session that asks one question at a time with a recommended answer, looks up project facts instead of asking, waits for shared understanding before writing files, then emits a minimal schemaVersion 2 recipe at .harness/spec.yaml with a baseline install command, plus .harness/prd.md and validators, leaving v2 defaults commented out.
assertions: The output satisfies: Follows grilling protocol: one question at a time / recommended answer
The output satisfies: Does not write files until shared understanding is confirmed
The output includes schemaVersion: 2: Recipe declares schemaVersion 2
The output includes .harness/spec.yaml: Writes the recipe to the project-centric .harness/ path
The output satisfies: Baseline includes a command literally named install
The output satisfies: Leaves v2-defaulted plumbing out of the recipe rather than restating it
The output satisfies: Does not emit keys removed in schema v2 (seed, generator, logging, extend)
The output includes hedera-consensus-service: Recommends generator skill hedera-consensus-service for HCS
The output satisfies: Keeps the run blind / separates PRD from oracle
The output satisfies: States that authoring skills stay out of the generator skills list
The output satisfies: Names doctor and/or check-spec.sh as the completion criterion

evals.prompt: Deepen my existing proof-wall harness recipe to Tier 3. Derive acceptance contract assertions from the PRD journeys (browse without wallet; wallet-gated post).
evals.expected_output: An acceptance contract at .harness/acceptance-contract.json with numbered assertions carrying statement and howToVerify, a fail-closed evaluationRules posture, both contract and validator.enabled set in the recipe, and a reminder that the PRD must stay blind.
assertions: The output satisfies: Uses stable numbered assertion ids (C1, C2, ...)
The output includes howToVerify: Assertions carry concrete browser verification steps
The output satisfies: Enables both contract and validator.enabled — either alone is misconfigured
The output uses the v2 default acceptance contract path
The output satisfies: Acceptance contract keeps a fail-closed posture
The output satisfies: Reminds the user not to leak oracle detail into the PRD
The output satisfies: Does not hand-write validator CLI flags or model names; the agent preset owns those

evals.prompt: When should I enable chainValidation for my harness recipe, and what YAML fields do I need?
evals.expected_output: Explains that Tier 3.5 is opt-in and requires Tier 3, that network must be testnet, that an ECDSA operator is supplied through environment variables, and that assertions must be flagged executableWithTestSigner to actually transact.
assertions: The output includes chainValidation: Names the chainValidation block
The output satisfies: States the network must be testnet
The output satisfies: Operator credentials come from environment variables
The output satisfies: Calls out that the operator must be ECDSA, not ED25519
The output includes executableWithTestSigner: Links chainValidation to executableWithTestSigner assertions
The output satisfies: States that Tier 3.5 depends on Tier 3

evals.prompt: My .harness/spec.yaml has an extend.baseline block and no schemaVersion. I want to add a new page to the recipe — can you edit it for me?
evals.expected_output: Recognizes a v1 recipe, declines to hand-edit it into v2, and recommends running hedera-harness migrate first, then authoring against the migrated v2 result.
assertions: The output satisfies: Identifies the recipe as predating schema v2
The output includes hedera-harness migrate: Recommends the migrate command
The output satisfies: Declines to hand-convert v1 to v2
The output satisfies: Explains that extend.baseline becomes baseline

evals.prompt: I want the harness to build a whole HTS subscription feature: the token service layer, a management UI, and wallet-gated mint flows. Should that be one PRD or several?
evals.expected_output: Weighs a single PRD against ordered increments, recommends splitting only because this spans layers, explains that prd accepts a list delivered in order onto one branch, and that each increment must leave the app green because baseline and Tier 0-1 run per increment and the first failure stops the sequence.
assertions: The output satisfies: Explains that prd can be an ordered list of increments
The output satisfies: Each increment must leave the app green on its own
The output satisfies: A failing increment stops the sequence
The output satisfies: Orders increments by dependency, not size
The output satisfies: Increments deliver onto a single branch
